chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Monasticism which they innovated' [57:27]. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The night prayer (Salat al-Layl)'.

key_terms.ابْتَدَعُوهَا: They innovated it; introduced something new not previously prescribed.
key_terms.رَهْبَانِيَّةً: Monasticism; a state of religious devotion or asceticism, here interpreted as night prayer.
key_terms.رِضْوَانِ اللَّهِ: The pleasure of Allah; the goal of the devotional act.
key_terms.صَلَاةُ اللَّيْلِ: The night prayer; a voluntary supererogatory prayer performed at night.

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic term 'monasticism' (Rahbaniyyah) refer to in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reinterprets the Quranic concept of 'monasticism' (rahbaniyyah) not as a literal withdrawal from society, but as the spiritual discipline of night prayer (Salat al-Layl). This aligns with the Shia scholarly view that voluntary acts of worship, particularly those performed in solitude and devotion, constitute the true essence of the 'monasticism' innovated by early Muslims to seek divine pleasure.
